readings.title: A programme before the curtain
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Seabrook Theatre emailed a plain-language guide before a relaxed performance. It described the story, the interval and effects that might be loud. Some organisers feared that advance detail would spoil the experience. Audience feedback suggested that knowing what to expect allowed many people to enjoy the performance more comfortably. The guide remained optional, so visitors who preferred surprise did not need to read it. Staff also made printed copies available. The theatre learnt that equal enjoyment did not always mean giving everyone exactly the same preparation.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: The ramp at the wrong door
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A theatre installed a portable ramp at a side entrance and described the building as accessible. During a visit, an adviser found that the door was locked until a staff member could be located. The ramp itself worked, but the arrival process did not. Management added a clearly marked call point and assigned responsibility for responding before every performance. It also included the entrance in staff practice sessions. Access involved an entire sequence of actions, not just possession of one piece of equipment. The improvement depended on people knowing what to do when a visitor arrived.

readings.title: Listening after the show
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A theatre survey asked audience members to rate their evening from one to five. Most selected four, leaving staff unsure what to improve. The next survey added two short questions: what made the visit easy, and what caused difficulty? Several replies mentioned the small print on signs near the cloakroom. The theatre enlarged the signs, then asked whether the change helped. Numerical ratings still offered a broad indication, but comments pointed to a specific action. Feedback became more useful when it identified a part of the experience rather than only a general feeling.

readings.title: A rehearsal open to newcomers
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A drama group invited local residents to watch a rehearsal. At first the director explained technical terms throughout, interrupting the actors repeatedly. Visitors said they appreciated the explanations but found it hard to follow the scene. The group changed the format: a short introduction, an uninterrupted section and questions afterwards. Both actors and visitors preferred it. Opening a professional process to the public did not require explaining everything at the exact moment it happened. Choosing an appropriate time for explanation helped preserve the activity people had come to understand.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

Enjoying a performance involves more than seeing the stage. Finding the entrance, understanding the programme and feeling welcome all shape the experience. Changes that help one group of visitors may help many others too. The most useful improvements often begin with listening.
translation.referenceAnswer: 欣赏演出不仅仅是看见舞台。能否找到入口、读懂节目单以及感到受欢迎，都会影响观演体验。帮助某一群体的改变也可能帮助其他许多人。最有用的改进往往始于倾听。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Suggest ways to make a small theatre more welcoming to people with different needs. Explain how staff could learn from audience feedback.
writing.sampleAnswer: A small theatre can become more welcoming by considering the whole visit. Information about entrances, seating and loud effects should be available before booking. Signs inside the building should use clear print, and staff should know how to help visitors use accessible routes. An optional plain-language programme could help people prepare without requiring everyone to read it. After performances, the theatre should ask specific questions about what was easy and what caused difficulty. Comments may reveal a practical problem that a general satisfaction score misses. Staff should then explain which improvements they have made. Listening and responding consistently would show that accessibility is part of everyday service, rather than a promise attached to one piece of equipment.
writing.explanation: 范文供完成作答后对照。允许不同立场与例子；围绕题目要求论述清楚、理由充分、语言准确即可。

criteria.name: 任务完成与内容
criteria.description: 回应题目所有要求，观点明确，包含相关理由、具体例子或可行建议。

criteria.name: 组织与衔接
criteria.description: 结构清楚，信息顺序合理，句段衔接自然，格式符合写作目的。

criteria.name: 语言与表达
criteria.description: 词汇使用恰当，句式基本准确，表达清晰；错误按其对理解的影响扣分。

knowledgePoints: 英语写作：观点、建议与应用文
